title: A TQFT-based Platform for Efficient Computation of Knot Invariants
authors: Amena Al Rawi, Hisham Sati, Vivek Kumar Singh
abstract: We present an interactive web platform that unifies the construction Feynman ribbon diagrams (FRDs), the evaluation of higher-rank Chern--Simons knot invariants, and the identification of FRD-like knots at higher crossing numbers. These tree-structured diagrams naturally represent arborescent knots, which we refer to throughout as FRD-like knots. Within a single visual environment, users can construct an FRD as a tensor network, evaluate its associated Chern--Simons invariants, and use the resulting invariant data to distinguish and identify the corresponding knot. To our knowledge, this is the first platform to combine diagrammatic construction, tensor-network evaluation, invariant computation, and knot identification within a unified workflow.
summary: This paper introduces an interactive web platform that unifies knot diagram construction, tensor network evaluation via TQFT, and the computation of colored Chern-Simons invariants. It demonstrates that this framework can systematically classify arborescent knots by mapping their topology onto computable quantum invariants. This represents a significant computational advance in topological quantum field theory.
main_problem: The core problem is classifying knots in 3D space, which becomes computationally intractable as the crossing number increases.
main_result: The authors developed a unified web platform that uses Feynman ribbon diagrams (FRDs) and TQFT principles to compute strong knot invariants for arborescent knots up to at least 10 crossings.
method: They map the combinatorial structure of an FRD onto a tensor network calculation, evaluating it using techniques derived from Chern-Simons theory to yield colored quantum invariants.
model_or_system: The model is Knot Theory, specifically focusing on arborescent knots represented by Feynman ribbon diagrams (FRDs). The underlying physics framework is Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) applied via Chern-Simons theory.
key_observables: Colored quantum invariants (Laurent polynomials in q), which must remain invariant under Reidemeister moves, and the knot determinant.
important_parameters: The crossing number of the knot ($c(K)$); the structure parameters defining the two-vertex FRD ($\Gamma(A_1; p_{12}; A_2)$).
main_assumptions: The platform is currently restricted to tree-shaped (arborescent) FRDs, and while the computation engine is general, knot identification relies on matching computed invariants against a finite database.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the relationship between a knot's conventional projection, its representation as an FRD, and its corresponding TQFT tangle structure. Figure 3 details the two-vertex diagram structure.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of knot classification, proposes the TQFT/FRD framework, details the construction of the interactive web platform ('TQFT Knot Explorer'), presents the mathematical machinery for tensor network evaluation, and concludes with results on the completeness of the two-vertex diagram family up to 10 crossings.
why_interesting: While not directly about AMO systems, the use of tensor networks (a computational tool) derived from topological field theory provides a powerful analogy for calculating entanglement or correlation functions in quantum many-body systems where local structure dictates global properties.
